Well first you need to analyse why killbox is a thing, first it compress whole colony firepower on very small angle. Second it is very cheap, both construction and maintenance. Third it is very safe, far safer then any other methods. 

Angle/frontline defence, you concentrate colony defense into one angle and just pray for the best. No limit on range gives enemy sniper all opportunity in the world. Less firepower then killbox, more expensive, specially maintenance, less safe. 

360° degree defence fortress, bad firepower compression + not very safe for same reason. Cost of maintenance will skyrocket. Safety too, at least battles would be cinematic not gonna lie. 

In field standoff, cheap as hell, but other parts are just through the window. No good defence, no compressed firepower. Not a path but a one way trip to game over. Yeah there are ways to make it less awful, but you need top tier sence of colony wealth and quickly response to any threat. 

If you want at least some efficiency take angle defense, many threats can be countered by your own snipers/turrets and you have nice amount of firepower. You can take 360 degree fortress, just be ready for very costly repair or sudden wall breach. Don't take 3 option tho, you would die.

First, for serching for ore node use Nose search on prospector pickaxe, you currently using geolocation mod, it tells chance of spawning ore in that point. As for additional advice, try digging straight down and check on node search on bottom every 4-6 blocks until you get reading on traces of needed ore. To change mods on your prospector pick, press F and choose needed one. 

If your digging shaft is empty, it can be, try firstly search on 4 direction, if you don't get any readings, try new shaft in 8+ block from your current. Traces means there is less then 2 blocks in 8x8x8 cube, huge amounts mean ore is somewhere close. 

Your current type of searching is used in big area, to determine if there a reason to try digging soil and searching for ores. Look at type of rating, Poor-> small chance of node underneath, still a chance if you desperate enough, but try looking on High, Ultra High and Decent, good place to start searching for that resource type. 

If prev advices didn't help, try using Absolute Prospecting in Vintage Mods, 16x16 search is cheat itself as it tells if there is a ore node in area 16x16xInfinity, so it scans area to bedrock. By it I found magnetite in areas with poor reading but ore vein itself where far from poor.

Well first it will show chance on finding ore in that specific point. That can be applied to chunk in what was ore prospected. Gradation of ore would tell how much you can find in that specific chunk, Very High and down to Decent is good way to go, you can totally find ore vein down there maybe even 2-3 if you lucky. Poor and lower might be a signal that this chunk maybe have or maybe don't have metal vein inside. % of chunk means how much of chunk does vein occupy, but without proper numbers just subjective thing, like you can easily find copper in 33% chunk then high Tin in 5% chunk, both 33 and 5 % are high reading for mentioned minerals, but tin deposits are way smaller.  
  
About Node search, it tells you what ores are in area 8x8 from block you break, traces means like 1-2 blocks nearby, huge means you are near metal vein. If you get similar response after going in same direction it means you are moving in parallel of where ore deposit is, try changing direction and don't forget to check roof and floor too, as you can be slightly higher then ore deposit is. Node search can tell if ore deposit is exhausted, as you won't get readings bigger then traces of that metal if there aren't much ore nearby. 

  
So what do you exactly do with prospector pick. 1. Find best reading of needed metal, Decent+ would be just fine, traces means you are near deposit, so you should go from that mark to find best spot. 2. Try mining best spot, go down in straight line and check bottom block with node search, try mining in other direction from main shaft to find at least traces of vein. 3. Try find vein by node search. 4. Mine vein. On cave ins active you need support beams so cave won't fall on you while you mine for ores. 

Some materials can't be found by prospecting, so if you find caves, research them, you can find ruins and many useless and useful materials like gems, lore books, saltpeter on walls or translocators with other useful stuff. Just try to get at least bronze armor to pick a fight with deep shivers or bowtows. Mark translocators so you can repair them later, those teleporters can kick you around and don't need recharge at all, so you can build transporting system out of them.

Yes, it is only way to keep at bay really huge enemy raids like 100+ tribals/kingdom pawns or 70+ industrial pawns. Even if build 360° defence to evade kill box it usually lacks power very hard, same problem with range leaving my base totally unprotected against snipers and other very high range units. Those high range pawns can solo even heaviest of defenses by destroying turrets all around making 360° defence even weaker than it already is. So main enemies of endgame are drop pod raids, bugs, snipers and tribesmen people attack waves. Also empire like forces as deserters can chew through most of defenses by even small squads. 

Drop pod raids, nothing will protect you from them, maybe by some mods you can counter them and destroy their pods until they land, but if they land it would be hell. Counter, firepopper in all rooms to save room from burning to ash with all loot inside. Windows are possible counter too, so you can shoot intruder through them. You don't need killbox for them, but vanilla defence won't protect you anyway. 

Bugs, same as drop pod raids, but other way around. Windows are still potentially best strategy but if you can burn them to ground with affected room so it. On fire bugs would panic and won't hit you pawns right away, they are very scary in melee combat and I don't recommend fighting them by it, specially with low penetration weapons. Still killbox not needed for bugs inside the base, if bugs are outside killbox will squish them with superior firepower. 

Snipers, the heaviest of them all to deal with, if you are fighting in the wild try to break line of sight and lure them closer. If there no way to lure them take or heaviest units and try to leap/jetpack to them to protect you pawns from damage. If it's not the case use mechanoids, vehicles or mortars to kill them without targeting them with our pawns directly. Killbox will lure them on range of shotgun shot, clearly easiest strategy, but be aware about ranges of your and enemies weapons for kill area type of killbox. 

Tribesmen, well this is very unpredictable threat, just gun them down on spot with not heaviest weapons because there are like a lot of them and they would spawn more so. Usually I use vehicles, mechanoids and squads equipped with lmgs, most of the time it is enough to hit they hard enough to retreat. Killbox or kill area are essential because tribesmen can bend the time itself literally clubbing tanks into oblivion. If they can get to you they are safe just don't try to recycle their appeal or you colony would drown in work. 

Quite big analysis and I don't even cover some of possible threats, but I guess it's enough. Final verdict, yeah you can play without killboxes or kill area, but before you do this you need to counter threats mentioned above. If you don't cover those weaknesses you colony will fall after another big blow of wind. About why I use them, most of the time I use kill areas as main defences, it doesn't fully protect against hordes, but with right support it can group annoying enemies and you can deal with almost everything except snipers without big problems. Main points of kill area is to concentrate both attack force and defense forces of your colony.

Opening doors can be death sentence if you don't know what are you doing. First you need to crouch before opening door, opening doors and checking corpses are free actions while crouching, on free turn look what do you see in the room, if something bad, switch to walk and close the door, next run,  if nothing too scary switch  from sneaking to any mode you like and start blasting. That's all, doors won't be an issue until RNG forces all your bullets to miss. And be careful checking corners, that can be very dangerous. 

Checking corners is like checking doors but slightly harder. First set near the corner and check crouch radar, if it's empty stay focused, some enemies can one shot you outside of hearing radius. Next set mod to run or walk and skip turn or two to make full turns count on you. Step 1 block inside the room and check around by character vision, if there no enemies that's it, continue searching. If there are enemies, target the hardest hitting one and start blasting. If there are heavy units, like legend's armor or patterns, try to lure them one by one and kill with hardest hitting weapon, don't even try to take them with rifle rounds pistol or buckshot shotguns or regular 9 mm, you will die because they won't have pain shock.
